lines.text: Pre and post contact characterization of electro-adhesive pressure with submillimeter interdigitated electrodes.
Authors: Sylvain Schaller and Prof. Herbert Shea
This README presents the structure of the data acquired for this paper and an explanation of the namings of the different files.
Structure:
A) ElectroAdhesion force measurements
I) Conductive object
csv files of measurements
II) Dielectric object
csv files of measurements
B) ACDC Adhesion, releasing, residual pressure results
csv files of measurements
the format for csv files measurements is the following:
Ex: 1_A1_20um_20um_6um_0.00V_cond_AC_sym_5.00Hz_0sdelay
"1": index of the patch on the wafer
"A1": id of wafer based on designed A
"20um": width of interdigitated electrodes on the patch
"20um": gap between interdigitated electrodes on the patch
"6um": thickness of the insulating material (P(VDF-TrFE-CTFE))
"0.00V": Voltage
"cond": measure on conductive object
"AC": AC signal supplied
"sym": the signal was symetric
"5.00Hz": frequency
"0sdelay": the delay once the contact is made between the patch and the object is 0 second
On each csv file, we recorded 3 informations corresponding respectively to the 3 columns in the file:
- The relative time value. On the graphs we rescaled every time period to start at 0 by subtracting the first time value on every lines.
- The relative position of the sensor (object). Again we rescaled it to 0 for the position.
- The force value where positive value correspond to tension stress (EA force) of the sensor and negative value to compression stress (when the sensor is pushing on the patch).
We computed and used the pressure value by dividing the value by 25 corresponding to the surface of the object (25 mm2)
The data labeled at 0.00 V correspond to the measurement at 0V done BEFORE the voltage measurement in order to ensure that no residual pressure would influence the measurement.
The one labeled at 1.00 V correspond to the measurement at 0V done AFTER the voltage measurement in order to record residual pressure.

grammar: Only CRLF/CR/LF delimit lines; VT/FF/NEL/U+2028/U+2029 remain literal. No fictitious empty line after final delimiter; blank delimited lines preserved.
